title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
abstract: arXiv:2608.19760v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audited against causal ground truth from executed replay in a single-agent tool environment (ALFWorld), none of the step-level credit signals used to train LLM agents -- LLM-judge scores, outcome-conditioned logprob ratios, or the policy's own confidence -- identifies which steps causally matter better than chance. Existing evaluations grade these signals against annotated step *correctness*; we audit them against step *contribution* -- what re-sampling the policy's own alternatives at each decision point and rolling forward actually changes about the outcome -- and the two come apart. The ground truth itself is structured: causal contribution is sparse (30.5% of decision points where ground truth is defined carry measurable effect), and measurability is model-dependent -- the fraction of points with no policy-supported counterfactual differs by a factor of two (13.1% vs. 26.8%) between two similar-scale policies. tldr: 本研究通过执行回放生成因果真实标签，审计发现现有步骤级信用信号在LLM智能体中无法有效识别因果关键步骤，且因果贡献稀疏且依赖模型，揭示了信用分配评估的根本缺陷。
en_tdlr: This study audits step-level credit signals in LLM agents against causal ground truth from executed replay, finding none outperform chance in identifying causally critical steps, with sparse and model-dependent causal contributions exposing fundamental flaws in credit assignment evaluation.
